description: gitIgnoredAuthors: .github/workflows/renovate-hashes.yml pushes a fetch-hash fixup commit onto renovate/** branches (#625). Renovate treats a branch carrying a commit by anyone but itself as edited by a human and stops updating it, so without this entry a newer release would never reach an already-opened PR.

packageRules.description: Auto-merge low-risk updates (patch versions + first-time digest pinning) after CI green; content-changing image digest refreshes are left manual for review.
Label content-changing image digest refreshes so the pr-aging workflow can identify them; kept manual (not in the auto-merge rule).

Container registries other than Docker Hub (ghcr.io, lscr.io) don't expose a per-tag publish time, so Renovate leaves releaseTimestamp unset for those images. Renovate's default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour is 'timestamp-required', which treats an unknown age as 'not yet aged' — combined with the top-level internalChecksFilter 'strict' that withholds those updates forever rather than for 7 days, silently freezing every ghcr.io/lscr.io image (this is what stalled bookorbit at 2.3.0 for a month). Scope 'timestamp-optional' to the docker datasource so a missing timestamp means 'can't measure, let it through' instead of 'block indefinitely'. Images whose age IS known (Docker Hub) still serve the full 7-day cooldown, and non-docker datasources keep the strict default.

The pkgs.caddy.withPlugins hash is regenerated in CI now (.github/workflows/renovate-hashes.yml), but caddy is the ingress every host's apps sit behind, so plugin bumps still get a human look before merge.

Home Assistant custom-component bumps get their fetchFromGitHub hash regenerated in CI (.github/workflows/renovate-hashes.yml), but a new component release can pin a different version of a python lib nixpkgs doesn't package (blueair-api, hoymiles-wifi in modules/apps/homeassistant.nix) — still a hand edit; keep manual and grouped.
Group Nix release-channel bumps and keep them manual.

customManagers.description: Update Docker image tags in Nix files (image = "repo:tag")
Update Docker image digests in Nix files (image = "repo:tag@sha256:...")
Update Caddy plugin versions in Nix files ("module@version")

Update fetchFromGitHub tags in Nix files (Home Assistant custom components). The match spans the renovate comment through the `tag` line, so the one version number written twice — `version` and `tag` — is rewritten in a single edit (autoReplaceGlobalMatch defaults to true, replacing every occurrence inside the match). It stops short of `hash`, which no string substitution can derive: CI regenerates that (.github/workflows/renovate-hashes.yml). extractVersionTemplate strips the tag's `v` so `version` stays a bare version, and the {1,7} line bound keeps a match from running past its own component into the next one's `tag`.

Update fetchFromGitHub rev pins in Nix files, for sources whose upstream re-cuts tags in place (dahlb/ha_blueair). currentDigest is the immutable commit the tag currently points at; currentValue is the component's own `version`, which the same match rewrites — so there is no trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment left to drift, which is precisely what went stale in #606. github-tags carries the commit sha on each release, so stripping the `v` via extractVersionTemplate doesn't cost the digest lookup. The match stops short of `hash`; CI regenerates that (.github/workflows/renovate-hashes.yml).
